newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks close month on firm note.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks close month on firm note.

text.p: Argentine stocks lost some steam but managed their fourth consecutive gain on Friday, dealers said.
Share prices were seen pushing higher thanks to bullish forecasts for the heavyweight telephone sector.

"The telephone stocks have gained a new lease on life with last night's tariff changes. This should keep the whole bolsa in positive territory even if there's selective profit-taking, like today," Jorge Bonanno at Interfin traders said.
The blue-chip MerVal index closed up 0.5 percent at 692.51, stretching the week's rise to 4.6 percent.
The MerVal showed a 6.6 percent gain for January and stood almost at a three-year high after the close on Friday.
"The market regrouped a bit today but it should easily conquer the 700 mark next week and head towards 730, where it peaked in 1994," another trader said.
Strong January tax revenue forecasts by private analysts were also seen underpinning the bolsa.

"If tax collection finally starts to grow the markets will get a huge boost, because it means the government will need to take on less loans to finance its huge debt burden and economic fundamentals will be solid," said Bonanno.
He said a stubborn fiscal gap was the weak point of Argentina's nine-month economic recovery.
The broad market closed up 1.3 percent Friday, with winners beating losers 40 to 17 and 22 issues closing unchanged.
Floor volume remained healthy but eased to 28.2 million pesos from 30.2 million on Thursday, while over-the-counter deals totaled 151.9 million pesos against 159.9 million on Thursday.
Gains were driven by Telecom and Telefnica, which benefitted from a raft of upgrades by international brokers and closed up 4.7 percent and 3.4 percent, respectively.
The rally came after the government on Thursday night announced cuts in long-distance and internatinoal telephone rates.

Other top MerVal gainers were power utilities Central Costanera and Central Puerto, which jumped 3.6 percent and 2.0 percent, respectively. Banco Francs rose 1.3 percent, and real estate developer Irsa added 1.1 percent.
Declining issues were led by foods company Molinos, construction stock Polledo and petrochemical concern Ipako, which pulled back 2.2 percent, 1.9 percent and 1.3 percent, respectively.
